formation.explanation: The leader appends each accepted command as a local log entry for its term (b-dispatch-logs), then each per-peer replication goroutine pushes AppendEntries and reports the highest index the peer has stored (b-leader-replicate). commitment.match/recalculate turn those per-voter match indexes into a quorum index, refusing to commit anything below the first index appended in the leader's term (b-commit-quorum). When the quorum index advances, the leader loop publishes the new commit index and applies the committed prefix (b-leader-commit-apply). The support is 'qualified' because a match index only counts after the follower's log has been shown to agree with the leader's up to the previous entry.

context.explanation: Authority is scoped to a term and to the voter set of the latest configuration. A follower that stops hearing a leader becomes a candidate (b-heartbeat-timeout); the candidate proposes and persists the next term and asks for votes, optionally after a pre-vote round (b-candidate-election, b-prevote), and becomes leader only on a quorum of current voters. Voters decide with term, membership, an already-persisted vote for the term, and log up-to-date-ness (b-vote-grant). A leader abandons the role when it observes a higher term or cannot contact a quorum of current voters (b-leader-stepdown), and it can hand the role over deliberately with a replicated-then-TimeoutNow transfer (b-leadership-transfer).

connection.explanation: A1 and A2 meet on three sourced points. First, the term-start-index rule in the commitment makes the leader's own new-term entry a precondition for committing anything, so a server that merely won an election cannot commit an earlier leader's entries (b-commit-quorum / f-commit-quorum / f-term-vote). Second, the voter set that defines both a winning quorum and the commitment quorum comes from the latest configuration, so membership changes reshape eligibility and commitment together (b-config-change, b-candidate-election / f-config-membership). Third, a follower only counts as support after its log prefix has been shown to match the leader's, and that same AppendEntries handling carries the term/state transitions; losing the term (b-leader-stepdown) discards the commitment that the old term's support created, while a transfer pushes the target to the leader's last index before handing over. Old work is handled by failing every inflight future with ErrLeadershipLost on step-down, so pending client requests cannot be mistaken for applied decisions.

open_details: The heartbeat fast path (Raft.processHeartbeat, installed by NewRaft and dispatched from NetworkTransport.handleConn) runs appendEntries off the main loop for pure heartbeats; the fields touched are atomic or lock-protected but the ordering against the main loop is unverified.
Raft.timeoutNow campaigns on the target without consulting the request term or sender.
The membership-change error path in appendConfigurationEntry continues to publish the new latest configuration and commitment after a StoreLogs failure that already set state Follower.
core_overview.rationale: Both core lines are read end to end from the leader's append/commit path and from the follower/candidate/voter/step-down path, and their three concrete connections (term-start-index commitment rule, configuration-driven quorum, prefix-validated support with pending-work failure on step-down) are sourced. The remaining items are local anomalies rather than unexplained formation or authority transitions, so the overview is usable while those leads stay open.

question.question: Does a node that committed a configuration whose entry was never stored still report that configuration as its latest configuration after a restart over the same stores, or does it re-derive only the configuration its log encodes?
question.importance: The configuration a node reports after recovery defines the voter set it will use for quorum, election eligibility and the leader lease for the rest of its life; if the in-memory anomaly persisted across a restart the divergence would become durable behaviour, while if only the log-backed configuration survives then the anomaly is confined to the running instance and the log remains the source of truth.

surfaces.reason: The transport heartbeat fast path invokes this handler outside the main loop: NewRaft installs it with trans.SetHeartbeatHandler, and NetworkTransport.handleConn (started with 'go') calls the handler directly for pure heartbeats. Raft.appendEntries is documented as main-thread only, though only pure heartbeats reach it and the fields they touch are individually serialized. The shutdown branch returns without answering the request: an exploration observed the same heartbeat answered immediately while the node ran and unanswered within the observation window after a clean shutdown.
Handles a TimeoutNowRequest by clearing the leader and campaigning; the request's term and sender are not consulted, which is recorded as an open premise of b-leadership-transfer.

Transport-level plumbing that decides whether a request is fast-pathed to the beacon handler or delivered on the consumer channel; it is not itself a consensus obligation, and its response wait after a fast-path request selects only on the response channel or its own shutdown, with no deadline, so a handler whose Raft instance has shut down stays parked until the transport stops.

A separate Go module that replaces github.com/hashicorp/raft with this working copy and pulls a previous release plus an older tag, then exercises mixed-version clusters for rolling upgrades and pre-vote behaviour; it is test scaffolding for the library rather than a runtime protocol responsibility.

The offline recovery entry point has now been read: RecoverCluster refuses to run without existing state, restores the newest usable snapshot, applies the command entries of the log tail, writes a new snapshot carrying the supplied configuration at configuration index 1, and deletes the whole stored log range so stored configuration entries cannot interfere; BootstrapCluster remains the fresh-cluster seeding path.
